key_insight: In rotating turbulence, geostrophic vortices are sustained by inertial-wave Reynolds stresses, with cyclones growing stronger and more compact than anticyclones, while very rapid rotation can reduce rather than enhance two-dimensionalization.
engineering_relevance: The results help predict how rotation controls large-scale coherent vortices and angular-momentum transport in geophysical and rotating-engineering flows.
method: Direct numerical simulations of rotating turbulence
Comparison with Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes balance for large-scale flow
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulated flow data showing Reynolds-stress consistency with RANS balance, cyclone-anticyclone asymmetry, and a non-monotonic fraction of geostrophic energy versus rotation rate.
watch_item: The absorption and vortex-strength trends may depend on rotation regime and model resolution, so extrapolation to other forcing conditions or higher Reynolds numbers should be done carefully.
paper_title: Wave-driven geostrophic vortices in rotating turbulence
